gpuLeadQuarters.description: Quarters from a chip order being placed to the chips running in a data centre.

buildingLeadQuarters.description: Quarters from committing to a data-centre building to it being ready for chips.

computeCostShare.description: Share of an AI lab's revenue that is spent on renting compute. Starting guess; the Anthropic S-1 compute commitments versus revenue are the intended anchor but are not yet in the committed data.
computeCostShare.source: assumption — Anthropic S-1 commitments vs revenue, not yet in committed data; calibrated in Task 12

overExtrapolation.description: How strongly buyers extend recent spending growth into their plans (1 means they simply continue the latest growth rate).

expectationGain.description: How fast buyers update their expectations towards what they just saw each quarter (0 means never, 1 means fully).

hyperscalerAiCapexShare.description: Share of hyperscaler capital spending that goes to AI infrastructure rather than other uses.

chipShareOfAiCapex.description: Share of AI infrastructure capital spending that buys accelerator chips (the rest is buildings, power and networking).

nvidiaShareOfAccelerators.description: Nvidia's share of accelerator spending, with the rest going to custom chips and other vendors.

nvidiaAspUsd.description: Average selling price of one Nvidia accelerator-equivalent unit, used to turn dollars into units shipped.

nvidiaGrossMargin.description: Nvidia's gross margin on sales. Starting value is the midpoint of management's 71.0%–72.0% guidance for Q4 FY27 in the 8-K of 2026-11-17.
nvidiaGrossMargin.source: NVIDIA 8-K 2026-11-17 Ex 99.1 (Q3 FY27 press release) outlook, midpoint; calibrated in Task 12

bullwhipInventoryWeeks.description: Weeks of demand that buyers and suppliers try to hold as inventory; when demand stalls the excess is worked off.

bullwhipCorrectionRate.description: Share of the gap between actual and target inventory that is corrected each quarter.

gpuEconomicLifeQuarters.description: How long an accelerator stays economically useful before newer chips make it uncompetitive.

gpuAccountingLifeQuarters.description: The period over which owners depreciate accelerators in their accounts (six years).
gpuAccountingLifeQuarters.source: assumption — hyperscaler depreciation policy of about six years

labShareDrift.description: How quickly spending shifts between AI labs towards the ones with better results each quarter.

defaultRunwayQuarters.description: Cash runway (in quarters of obligations) below which a lab or cloud provider is treated as defaulting; 0 means cash must stay positive.

defaultContractQuarters.description: Typical length of a compute contract signed by a lab, used when a deal has no stated end date.

defaultLoanTermQuarters.description: Length of a loan or bond taken from a deal record that states neither an end date nor a term; the principal is repaid in full in its last quarter.
defaultLoanTermQuarters.source: assumption — five years, a common corporate term-loan and bond tenor; no committed source

aiAddressableWageBillUsd.description: Yearly wage bill of the work that AI could plausibly take over, the ceiling for labour-substitution spending. Rough placeholder, no committed source yet; refine from BLS or OECD figures.
aiAddressableWageBillUsd.source: assumption — rough placeholder; no BLS/OECD figure committed yet

cowosUnitsPerQuarter.description: Most accelerators that advanced chip packaging (CoWoS) can produce in a quarter. About 120k wafers a month at end-2026 x 3 months x ~12 packages per wafer x ~0.7 yield and mix.
cowosUnitsPerQuarter.source: secondary — research_notes existing_ai_models_data.md section 2 (JPM, TrendForce, EffectStory CoWoS estimates 105k–140k wpm); analyst estimates, conversion is a heuristic not verified

hbmUnitsPerQuarter.description: Most accelerators that high-bandwidth memory supply can feed in a quarter. No HBM bit-supply figure was retrieved in the research notes, so this is a placeholder set slightly above the packaging ceiling.
hbmUnitsPerQuarter.source: assumption — research notes found no 2026 HBM bit-supply figure (existing_ai_models_data.md section 2); placeholder

kwPerAccelerator.description: All-in facility power drawn per accelerator, including cooling and networking. Implied by Epoch: about 2 million accelerators drawing about 9 GW.
kwPerAccelerator.source: secondary — Epoch AI supercomputer trends via AI CERTs, in research_notes existing_ai_models_data.md section 1 (9 GW / 2M accelerators)

powerLoadFactor.description: Share of contracted data-centre power that is actually available to run accelerators at any time.

tsmcShareOfChipCost.description: Share of an accelerator's selling price that is paid to TSMC for wafers and packaging.

skHynixShareOfChipCost.description: Share of an accelerator's selling price that is paid to SK hynix for high-bandwidth memory.

asmlShareOfTsmcCapex.description: Share of TSMC's capital spending that goes to ASML lithography tools.

cloudOperatingCostRatio.description: Operating costs other than depreciation and interest (power, staff, leases) as a share of cloud-provider revenue.

labOperatingCostRatio.description: Operating costs of an AI lab other than compute (staff, sales, research) as a share of its revenue.

holdLastRangeK.description: Width of a hold-last condition range in standard deviations of its quarterly changes (1.645 gives a two-sided 90% band under a random walk).

holdLastVolLookbackQuarters.description: Number of most recent history quarters whose quarter-to-quarter changes set the volatility of a hold-last range.
holdLastVolLookbackQuarters.source: assumption — five years of quarterly history

trendDecayGrowthLookbackQuarters.description: Number of latest history steps averaged to get the starting growth rate of a trend-decay default path (1 = the latest quarter-on-quarter growth).

aiSpendLongRunQuarterlyGrowth.description: Long-run growth rate of frontier-lab revenue that the aiSpend default growth decays towards (0.04 a quarter is about 17% a year).
aiSpendLongRunQuarterlyGrowth.source: assumption — no published long-run lab revenue forecast in the committed data

aiSpendGrowthHalfLifeQuarters.description: Half-life of the gap between the latest observed aiSpend growth rate and its long-run rate in the trend-decay default.

aiSpendRangeLogA.description: Base half-width (log terms) of the aiSpend forecast range one quarter ahead; covers the missing OpenAI component and revenue-recognition differences.

aiSpendRangeLogB.description: Extra half-width (log terms) of the aiSpend forecast range for each further quarter ahead.

aiSpendNoDataUsdPerYear.description: Placeholder aiSpend used only when no Anthropic or company-stated OpenAI revenue point is known at the as-of date; the range source then says Assumption.
aiSpendNoDataUsdPerYear.source: assumption — order-of-magnitude placeholder, not data; the committed lab revenue data start with the OpenAI 2026-03-31 statement and the Anthropic S-1 (Oct 2026)

gpuResaleLongRunQuarterlyGrowth.description: Long-run quarterly change in the used-to-new price ratio once a GPU is no longer the frontier part; the gpuResale default decays towards it.
gpuResaleLongRunQuarterlyGrowth.source: derived from used-gpu-a100-80gb-yoy-amcompute (used A100 -33.5% in the year to Aug 2026): 0.665^(1/4) - 1 = -0.097; secondary

gpuResaleGrowthHalfLifeQuarters.description: Half-life of the gap between the latest observed gpuResale growth rate and its long-run rate in the trend-decay default.

gpuResaleRangeLogA.description: Base half-width (log terms) of the gpuResale range one quarter ahead, set from the spread of used H100 PCIe quotes.
gpuResaleRangeLogA.source: derived from used-gpu-h100-pcie-80gb-low/high-servnet (14,000 to 25,000 USD around a 19,500 midpoint: ln(25000/19500) = 0.25); secondary

gpuResaleRangeLogB.description: Extra half-width (log terms) of the gpuResale forecast range for each further quarter ahead.

gpuResaleNoDataFraction.description: Placeholder used-to-new GPU price ratio used only when no used and new GPU prices are public at the as-of date.

gpuRentalNoDataUsdPerGpuHour.description: Placeholder H100 reserved rental price used only when no SemiAnalysis reserved price is public at the as-of date.

gpuRentalFallbackQuarterlyLogVol.description: Quarterly volatility used for the gpuRental range when fewer than two history quarters are known.

labourSubstitutionNoDataPercent.description: Placeholder for the Ramp AI Index used only when no RAMPAIALL point is public at the as-of date (before Feb 2023).

labourSubstitutionFallbackQuarterlyVol.description: Quarterly volatility used for the labourSubstitution range when fewer than two history quarters are known.

powerGwNoData.description: Placeholder global data-centre capacity used only when no IEA data-centre electricity figure is public at the as-of date (before Apr 2025).

powerRangeLogA.description: Base half-width (log terms) of the powerGw range around the published IEA path.

powerRangeLogB.description: Extra half-width (log terms) of the powerGw range per quarter away from the as-of date, calibrated to the LBNL 2024 report spread.
powerRangeLogB.source: derived from LBNL 2024 US Data Center Energy Usage Report: 2028 range 325–580 TWh is about ±0.29 log around its midpoint, 14 quarters after publication (Dec 2024): (0.29 - 0.05) / 14 = 0.017; secondary

tokenPriceIndexBase.description: Token price index level at the as-of quarter; the tokenPrice condition is an index with no committed price history.

tokenPriceQuarterlyLogVol.description: Quarterly volatility of the token price index used for its range; wide because published declines span 9x to 900x a year.
tokenPriceQuarterlyLogVol.source: assumption — informed by the Epoch-based 9x–900x a year decline range (research_notes existing_ai_models_data.md section 4)

priceElasticityDefault.description: Percent rise in AI usage for a 1% fall in token price (1 = unit elastic); no quantitative estimate was found in the research.
priceElasticityDefault.source: assumption — research_notes historical_analogs.md: no quantitative estimate of the elasticity of AI usage to token price was found

priceElasticityQuarterlyVol.description: Quarterly volatility used for the priceElasticity range around its assumed value.

physicalAiIndexBase.description: Physical-AI demand index level at the as-of quarter; there is no committed physical-AI revenue history to start from.

physicalAiQuarterlyLogVol.description: Quarterly volatility of the physical-AI demand index used for its range.

exportRegimeDefault.unit: regime code (1 open, 0.5 licensed with limits, 0 closed)
exportRegimeDefault.description: US export regime for AI chips to China; 0.5 = licensed with limits, the status as of Nov 2026 per the research notes.
exportRegimeDefault.source: assumption — research_notes existing_ai_models_data.md section 5 (Hopper shipments to China in Q3 FY27, H200 licences reportedly granted)

exportRegimeQuarterlyVol.description: Quarterly volatility used for the exportRegime range; the range is clipped to 0..1.

openingFactMaxStaleQuarters.description: Opening balances use the latest reported fact up to this many quarters older than the quarter before the start; an older fact is ignored and the balance is modelled. Covers companies whose latest 10-Q is not yet filed at the as-of date.

segmentShareConsumer.description: Share of end-customer AI spending that comes from consumers (subscriptions and apps).

segmentShareEnterprise.description: Share of end-customer AI spending that comes from businesses (enterprise seats and API usage).

segmentShareSovereign.description: Share of AI spending from governments and sovereign AI programmes outside the US and China.

segmentShareChina.description: Share of AI spending from China when exports are fully open; scaled by the export-policy condition.

segmentSharePhysicalAi.description: Share of AI spending on physical AI (cars, robots) at a physical-AI index of 1; this spend buys chips directly rather than lab services.

tokenPriceBase.description: Token price index level at which the AI-spend condition applies unchanged; elasticity scales spend relative to it.
tokenPriceBase.source: assumption — conditions express token price as an index of 1 at the as-of quarter

capexPerQuarterlyRentUsd.unit: USD of capex per USD of quarterly rent
capexPerQuarterlyRentUsd.description: How much a cloud invests to add capacity that earns one dollar of AI rent per quarter (roughly the payback period in quarters).

customChipShareOfBudget.description: Share of Alphabet's and Amazon's chip budget spent on their own designs (Google TPU with Broadcom, Amazon Trainium with Marvell) rather than NVIDIA or AMD.

maxLendingCreditSpread.description: Credit spread above which lenders stop extending new credit to debt-funded clouds in this simple phase-2 rule.
maxLendingCreditSpread.source: assumption — Baa spread peaked near 6 points in 2008-09 (FRED BAA10Y)

creditCapacityMultipleOfRent.unit: USD of new credit per USD of quarterly rent
creditCapacityMultipleOfRent.description: How much new debt a debt-funded cloud can raise in a quarter, as a multiple of its quarterly rent revenue, when credit is open.

edgeNonAiQuarterlyUsd.description: NVIDIA Edge Computing revenue (PCs, gaming, cars, robots) held flat as a simple trend; physical-AI spend from the demand layer is added separately.
edgeNonAiQuarterlyUsd.source: NVIDIA 8-K 2026-11-17 CFO commentary: Edge Computing $8.2B in Q3 FY27 (includes some physical AI; overlap noted)

newLoanRateSpreadOverRiskFree.description: Extra interest over the 10-year Treasury plus the credit-spread condition that debt-funded clouds pay on new loans.
newLoanRateSpreadOverRiskFree.source: assumption — CoreWeave DDTL margins of SOFR+2.25% to +13% (data/deals/deals.json)

supplierOperatingCostRatio.description: Operating costs of chip suppliers (TSMC, SK Hynix, ASML) as a share of their revenue in this simple phase-2 rule.
